items.title: 'Why get up if you have nowhere to go?': NDIS participants slam cuts
items.description: NDIS participants set up their lives around the scheme's rules. But now the rules are changing and they fear what lies ahead.

items.title: Plan to end NDIS 'wild west' will flip rules on their head for providers
items.description: NDIS Minister Mark Butler will end the practice of handwritten invoices, providers without qualifications and a "let it rip" market of profiteering operators. But the sector warns changes must be navigated carefully.

items.title: Politically, baby boomers' day has come
items.description: The Albanese government is reading the room when it comes to intergenerational equity ahead of the May 12 budget.

items.title: Live: Trump says ceasefire between Lebanon and Israel extended for three weeks
items.description: Donald Trump says the US will work with Lebanon to "protect itself from Hezbollah" and that he will meet with Benjamin Netanyahu soon. Follow live.

items.title: What happened when I messaged the number threatening slain reporter
items.description: Talks in Washington are set against a backdrop of decades-long disputes and deep mistrust, but at least they're happening.

items.title: Live: Australia must 'get serious' about defence to be better ally to US, Hastie says
items.description: Liberal frontbencher Andrew Hastie uses a speech ahead of Anzac Day to warn Australia must bring more to its alliance with the US, and appreciate that it is a relationship built on strategic value, not sentimentality. Follow live.

items.title: 'Finfluencers' suspected of giving unlawful advice hit with warning notices
items.description: The warning notice to the so-called "finfluencers" relates to suspected provision of unlicensed financial advice, including promoting claims of guaranteed returns.

items.title: 'This is now terminal': UK braces for prospect of sixth PM in seven years
items.description: Sir Keir Starmer, who led Labour to a landslide general election victory in July 2024, has become so unpopular that even some colleagues are framing his demise as a case of not if, but when.

items.title: How Aussies near you are coping with the fuel crisis
items.description: Petrol prices are reshaping Australian life in ways big and small — from a grandmother's isolation to a farmer's future.

items.title: Live: Oil prices spike again just as Australian fuel prices drop
items.description: The price of unleaded petrol is back to just 10 cents a litre more than before the war, even as oil prices are spiking again on global markets. Follow the day's events and insights as they happen with our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: The legacy of once-banned soldiers that hides in plain sight
items.description: Thousands of Indian soldiers served alongside Anzac forces at Gallipoli, leaving their legacy in the "puggaree" — a traditional Indian headwrap that was adapted to adorn the slouch hats worn by the Australian army.

items.title: Ancient fossils reveal when the iconic Twelve Apostles formed
items.description: An analysis of tiny fossils of sea creatures found in rock samples around the Port Campbell region in south-western Victoria has refined our understanding of how the Twelve Apostles formed.

items.title: 'They deserve death': Officer used internal system to monitor police wife
items.description: Text messages read in court set out how a Tasmania Police officer monitored his wife's movements, including via an internal dispatching system, as part of a 15-month family violence matter.

items.title: US watchdog announces Epstein files audit
items.description: The audit follows months of controversy over censorship, missed deadlines and the publication of survivors' details.

items.title: Jane Fonda was in her 40s when she changed the way we exercise
items.description: In the 1980s, the fitness industry as we know it was just getting started. One of the most important people in developing the way we exercise today was Jane Fonda, who released a best-selling aerobics video in 1982.

items.title: Figure skating teen makes history for Australia
items.description: At just 15, Hana Bath became the first Australian female to ever land a triple axel in competition. The rising star now has her eye on the 2030 Winter Olympics.

items.title: Weekly news quiz: Trump's eleventh-hour announcement, a disabled bird and a speedy humanoid robot
items.description: It's Friday, and that means it's time to test your news knowledge from the past seven days. Were you paying attention this week?

items.title: Sheraz risked his life translating in Afghanistan. His family paid the price
items.description: Sheraz worked with Australian and US troops in Afghanistan, as a result his family were targeted by the Taliban. This Anzac Day he's being heroed.

items.title: Which states get a public holiday for Anzac Day?
items.description: Anzac Day is observed on April 25 every year. This year that date falls on a Saturday, but that doesn't mean a long weekend for everyone.

items.title: 'Genuinely speechless': Appeal board's stunning claim in homophobia case
items.description: The appeal board in the Lance Collard homophobia case says homophobic and racist language is commonplace in the AFL due to the "highly competitive" nature of the game.

items.title: Hackers steal $3.7m from Sri Lanka earmarked for debts to Australia
items.description: Cyber criminals have hacked Sri Lanka's finance ministry, stealing millions of dollars destined to repay Australia.

items.title: Charts explain why fertiliser prices aren't coming down anytime soon
items.description: Farmers around the world are going to be paying more for one of their most important inputs, fertiliser. Here are four charts that explain why.

items.title: Hundreds of fishing boats sit idle off southern China — but they're not there to fish
items.description: Off China's southern coast, hundreds of fishing boats sit idle. The crews aren't there to fish, but rather to "maintain presence" as part of a shadowy, state-funded fleet.

items.title: Adelaide Festival appoints new Writers' Week director in wake of crisis
items.description: The new director of Adelaide Writers' Week says she is hopeful "really important lessons have been learned" following the implosion of this year's literary festival.

items.title: Bulldogs offer update after star's horror fall as Curnow kicks a bag
items.description: Sydney's hold on top spot is strengthened by a 66-point win over the Western Bulldogs, whose injury woes continue.
